summary_one_line: parts.i upgraded to research solved (KLL 2025); parts.ii confirmed genuinely open with PRECISE quantitative gap identified: KLL gives S1 << log N / sqrt(log log N), need S1 << log N / (log log N)^(1+eps) to close via Abel summation. Conditional reduction lemma added to Lean file.

headline_contribution.what_we_did_NOT_do: We did not solve parts.ii. It is an open Erdős problem and remains so.
what_we_DID_do: Upgraded parts.i status from research open to research solved (matching KLL 2025 literature).

Identified and formalized the PRECISE quantitative gap blocking parts.ii: KLL's S1 bound has loglog exponent 1/2; the threshold for Abel-summation closure of parts.ii is loglog exponent (1+eps). One loglog factor short.
Added a conditional reduction lemma `parts_ii_of_strengthened_S1` to 143.lean that states: if S1 bound is strengthened to log N / (log log N)^(1+eps), then parts.ii follows.
Numerical evidence at scale: greedy-random near-WS set of 2000 elements up to N=10^10 yields S2 ≈ 0.22, stable across six decades — strongly consistent with summability.

decisions: parts.i: solved by KLL (literature confirms density-zero result, not just o(log n)); upgrade status, body stays sorry per formal-conjectures convention.
parts.ii: identify and formalize quantitative gap via Abel summation. Document in docstring AND add conditional reduction lemma.
Reject: do not dispatch Codex/Athena on parts.ii proper. KLL is state of the art; a session-scale attempt has near-zero success probability.

analytical_threshold_derivation.abel_summation: S2(N) = S1(N)/log N + ∫_2^N S1(t) / (t (log t)^2) dt

with_strengthened_S1_log_t_over_loglog_t.integral: ≪ ∫ dt/(t log t (log log t)^(1+eps)); change of variables u = log t, then v = log u, gives ∫ dv / v^(1+eps), converges for eps > 0

with_KLL_actual_S1_log_t_over_sqrt_loglo.integral: ≪ ∫ dt/(t log t sqrt(log log t)); change of variables gives ∫ dv/sqrt(v), DIVERGES like 2 sqrt(v) = 2 sqrt(log log x)

analytical_threshold_derivation.gap: KLL is sqrt-of-loglog away from sufficient. Specifically, need to improve loglog exponent from 1/2 to 1+eps — a strengthening of (log log N)^{1/2 + eps}.

changes.parts_i: research open → research solved, answer(sorry) → answer(True), docstring cites KLL and disclaims naive dyadic-block argument
changes.parts_ii: docstring rewritten with precise quantitative gap (KLL exponent 1/2 vs sufficient exponent 1+eps); status remains research open
changes.lemmas_parts_ii_of_strengthened_S1: NEW conditional reduction lemma added. Hypothesis: ∃ ε > 0, ∀ WS A, S1 = O(log N / (log log N)^(1+ε)). Conclusion: ∀ WS A, Σ 1/(x log x) < ∞. Body is sorry; docstring contains Abel-summation proof sketch and clearly labels hypothesis as 'currently open'.

round_1_findings: Caught flawed dyadic-block proof sketch in parts.i lemma (later removed)
Confirmed parts.ii is genuinely stronger than KLL
round_2_findings: KLL's quantitative bound is S1 ≪ log x / sqrt(log log x)
Abel-summation against this gives S2 ≪ sqrt(log log x) — UNBOUNDED in principle
To force S2 finite need S1 ≪ log x / (log log x · (log log log x)^(1+eps)) or simpler-form S1 ≪ log x / (log log x)^(1+eps)
No follow-up paper has achieved this
No known counterexample, no known proof — parts.ii is precisely at the edge of current methods

publishable_claims: Erdős Problem 143 part (i) is tagged 'research solved' in DeepMind formal-conjectures, with attribution to KLL 2025.
Erdős Problem 143 part (ii) remains open. The Abel-summation analysis pinpoints the precise quantitative gap blocking a proof: KLL's exponent 1/2 in (log log N)^{1/2} must be strengthened to 1+ε.
A conditional reduction `parts_ii_of_strengthened_S1` is added to the Lean file, expressing this gap formally for future formalization work.
next_actions: Decide whether to commit 143.lean to branch codex/erdos143-formal-conjectures-kll and open upstream PR (Publisher gate first since this is a public-repo PR).
Research question for parts.ii (not session-scale): can KLL's GCD-graph framework be sharpened from sqrt(log log N) to (log log N)^(1+ε)? This is exactly one notch above current state of the art.
Alternative research direction: structural argument that bypasses Abel summation entirely (e.g., via energy estimates on the GCD graph or multiplicative-energy decomposition).
